program_name: Economics and Strategies for International Markets
campus: Bari, Department of Economics and Finance; ESMI-EGEI includes consortium mobility locations
academic_year: [uncertain] 2025/2026 programme regulations; programme listed in the 2026/2027 international offer
academic_requirements: A bachelor's degree or another foreign qualification recognized as equivalent is required.
Holders of Italian degree classes L-18, L-33, L-41 or L-36 may enter without demonstrating additional curricular credits.

Applicants from other degree classes must meet the specified economics, business and statistics credit requirements before enrolment; the programme council may evaluate course syllabi when the recorded credits are below the nominal thresholds.
Admission to the international ESMI-EGEI curriculum is additionally governed by the Erasmus Mundus consortium Partnership Agreement and Grant Agreement.
qualification_system_requirements: A suitable first-cycle foreign qualification must be recognized as equivalent and must provide access to master's-level study in its system of origin.
eligible_degree_classes: L-36 Political Science and International Relations
Other classes or foreign equivalents meeting the curricular requirements

required_subject_credits.ssd_or_domain: ECON-01/A Political Economy (formerly SECS-P/01) and ECON-02/A Economic Policy (formerly SECS-P/02)
required_subject_credits.notes: Applies to applicants outside the directly eligible degree classes who lack the curricular requirements.

required_subject_credits.ssd_or_domain: ECON-06/A Business Administration (formerly SECS-P/07) and ECON-07/A Management (formerly SECS-P/08)
required_subject_credits.notes: Applies to applicants outside the directly eligible degree classes who lack the curricular requirements.

required_subject_credits.ssd_or_domain: STAT-01/A, STAT-02/A, STAT-03/A or STAT-03/B (formerly SECS-S/01, SECS-S/03, SECS-S/04 or SECS-S/05)
required_subject_credits.notes: Ten CFU in the statistical area.

language_requirements: English proficiency of at least CEFR B2 is required for admission to the degree.
The standard ESMI curriculum is taught in Italian; non-EU students resident abroad enrolling in the Italian-taught route must meet UNIBA's Italian-language test or exemption rules.
The ESMI-EGEI curriculum is taught in English and is subject to the consortium's admission rules.
language_level: B2 English; B2 Italian is an exemption level for the Italian-language test applicable to the Italian-taught route
accepted_language_evidence: [uncertain] Programme council verification of adequate English knowledge
Recognized Italian B2-or-higher certificates such as CILS, CELI, Roma Tre or PLIDA for exemption from the Italian test on the Italian-taught route
personal_preparation_assessment: The Programme Council verifies curricular fit by reviewing prior coursework and syllabi and checks adequate English knowledge before authorizing enrolment. [uncertain] The current public regulation does not state a fixed interview format or calendar. ESMI-EGEI applicants are assessed under the consortium agreement.
ofa_or_remedial_obligations: Missing curricular requirements must be completed before enrolment through single-course or extracurricular coursework; master's enrolment cannot proceed while prerequisites remain unmet.
